In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the opioid‐addict patient with cancer can be treated with narcotics, but that the clinician must be aware of the potential problems that may be encountered.
the use of opioids for the treatment of pain in cancer patients with a history of opioid addiction should be approached in the same way as for any other patient.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

pain management in the opioid addicted patient with cancer can be successfully achieved with careful attention to the patient’s psychological needs, proper dosing of analgesics, and appropriate use of contract therapy.
pain management in the opioid addict is possible with careful assessment of pain, attention to proper dosage, and appropriate psychological and social support.

the use of opioids in the opioid‐abused patient with cancer is safe and effective if proper precautions are taken to ensure that the patient is not abusing the medication and if the patient is monitored for signs of disease progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of opioids in opioid‐addicted patients with cancer should be approached with caution, and that a multidisciplinary approach is required for successful pain management in these cases.
patients with a history of opioid abuse should not be denied pain control for their cancer pain.
pain management in the opioid-addicted patient with cancer can be challenging but not impossible.
